text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said on Wednesday it has started operating a Boeing 757-200 freighter service between its Middle East hub in Bahrain and its European hub in Brussels.
The 38-tonne capacity freighter flies six times a week between the hubs, DHL Gulf states general manager Ken Pascoe told a news conference at the 18th Air Cargo Forum.

Five of the six weekly flights stop in Bergamo in northern Italy, where DHL has a 'sub-hub' operation, he said. From here, DHL services cities across northern Italy, Switzerland, Austria, southern France, Germany and Spain.
Pascoe said DHL took over the lease for the 757, which is owned by Australia's Ansett Worldwide from Gulf Air.

He said DHL was evaluating possible flights to other Gulf cities, including Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates. On November 14, DHL would take over its new airside facility in the Dubai Airport Free Zone, he added.
The Regional Distribution Centre in Bahrain processes 1,500 packages and 6,000 documents per hour.
"Heavier consignments are recording the strongest growth, whether coming into or leaving this region," DHL said in a statement.
Pascoe said shipments in the UAE were up 30 percent so far this year and revenue was around 20 percent higher.
